calls.reason: The AIMultiple benchmark (15–60% errors on supplied CNN articles) supports the reliability half. No evidence backs the half-trillion cumulative cost, and the IEA and Stanford figures measure different things.

The April 23, 2025 Wikipedia revision's introduction lists nationality, LA birth, the Spinal Tap co-writing credit, SNL, the named films, radio, awards and spouse. That is most of the listed items, with only a few further down.

The Cohn study found voice, not wording, raised anthropomorphism. The Turing-test study measures mistaking a bot for a human, not beliefs about how LLMs work inside. Neither settles the claimed cause.

Kagi's puzzle benchmark shows illegal-move rates from 0.9% to over 80%, with no full-game test. Karvonen's chess-trained model learned board representations, which weakens the claimed lack of abstractions.
OpenAI's April 2025 system card shows its models answering about 20–59% of SimpleQA and PersonQA questions correctly, with hallucination rates of 16–79%. That is often right but routinely wrong.

The Scientific Reports study and the Mata v. Avianca order document fabricated references, and OpenScholar shows retrieval improves scholarly citation accuracy. Nothing establishes a shared cause across scholarly and legal fabrications.
